svg.title: A stateless deployment, with the session store crossed out
svg.desc: Four columns. On the left, three hosts, each holding one client: a desktop host, an editor host and your own command line tool. Their arrows join one bus into the second column, where an ingress terminates Transport Layer Security, validates the Origin header, and rate limits by reading the Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers, and feeds a plain round-robin balancer beneath it that parses no bodies and configures no affinity. Below the balancer, still at full size and still in its old place, sits a dashed box labelled session store, sticky routing and Mcp-Session-Id, struck through twice in red. Beside the cross, three lines say what is gone and cite it: no Mcp-Session-Id from SEP-2567, no initialize handshake from SEP-2575, and no in-flight state across a round trip from SEP-2322. The third column holds three replicas of the same image with the same configuration, one on each host row, fed from a single bus so that any of them can answer any request. The fourth column holds the two things that are allowed to keep state: a backend, described as the only thing here with state in it, and an observability sink taking standard error lines and spans over OTLP. A band across the foot says the balancer never opens the body, because SEP-2243 mirrors the routing-relevant fields into headers, and that a header disagreeing with the body earns a 400 response carrying error -32020. Two closing lines note that the backend is still stateful and that this is fine, because the protocol stopped adding a second separate kind of state on top of it, and that scaling is one flag on docker compose with nothing else to change.
svg.text: Nothing to pin, so nothing to configure
Every request carries its own version and capabilities, so any replica can answer any request.
no in-flight state across a round trip
The balancer never opens the body
SEP-2243 mirrors the routing-relevant fields into headers: Mcp-Method on every request, Mcp-Name on
tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get. Disagree with the body and the server answers 400 with -32020.
The backend is still stateful, and that is fine. The protocol stopped adding a second, separate kind of state on top of it.
Scale by adding replicas: docker compose up --scale system-info=3, and there is nothing else to change.
